_note: Stock resources: physical goods, stored and hauled by hand. Failure is slow and visible in advance — which is what gives the player time to make political choices, and where dilemmas come from. haulable=false marks goods consumed where they are made.

stocks.name: Food
stocks.description: Rations from the hydroponics bays and the protein vats, served in the canteens. It rots in store, slower where food processing works.

quote.text: It's called protein because nobody would queue for something called vat.

stocks.name: Scrap
stocks.description: Metal salvaged from the Shaft's own leftovers. The recycler melts it back into steel, and the protein vats take a little for reasons nobody explains.

quote.text: One man's scrap is another man's staircase. Please stop taking the staircase.

stocks.name: Wood
stocks.description: Grown in the grove, at a real cost in water and space. Nobody needs it to live; everyone wants it in their suite. Pulped into paper.

quote.text: A tree down here is either a luxury or a political statement. Usually both.

stocks._note: Deliberately NOT survival-critical, which is what makes spending Cultivation slots on it a political statement. The political layer literally consumes it — see the paper recipe.

stocks.name: Paper
stocks.description: Pressed from wood at the workshop. The political layer runs on it: Accord amendments, court records, the archive's shelves.

quote.text: Every law in the Shaft started as a tree, and some of them still have the knots.

stocks.primaryUse: Accord amendments, archives, court records, the Apocrypha's volumes
stocks._note: A Chair who legislates constantly is quietly spending the Shaft's timber. A Shaft that can no longer make paper can no longer keep records.
